appShellRepository.getNavigation is the only exported data entry point; it awaits the api and returns mapNavigationFromApi's output, typed Promise<Navigation>. app-shell.repository.spec.ts crosses the seam with vi.spyOn on the api boundary and asserts the whole ViewModel with toStrictEqual.

git grep -ln api-model over apps/web/src returns only api/navigation.api.ts, app-shell.mapper.ts, app-shell.mapper.spec.ts (the repository hit is the literal inside its own comment, read with comments in view — not an import). No route, loader, component or .pod.tsx imports an api-model or the mapper.

Mapper renames full_name/avatar_url/cover_url, drops email and derives initials. Verified at the real SSR boundary, not asserted: the served HTML of the 404 carries 0 occurrences of email, sofia.martin@, full_name, avatar_url, cover_url and 0 ISO date strings, while initials, avatarUrl, coverUrl x4 and "SM" are present. app-shell.mapper.spec.ts covers 5 degenerate name forms including empty and whitespace-only.

Every intra-pod import is relative ('./app-shell.model', './api/navigation.api'); the #/ alias appears only where the pod crosses into common/ (mock-data in api/, components in the pod). git grep -rn '#/pods' apps/web/src/pods returns nothing.
No cross-pod import exists: not-found.pod.tsx imports only from #/common/*, and app-shell.pod.tsx only from #/common/* plus its own relative model.
File-name audit of the diff: .component.tsx on bottom-nav/side-nav, .pod.tsx on app-shell and not-found, framework filenames kept for routes/_app.tsx and routes/_app/$.tsx.

Enforced by the file tree, not a conditional: _app/$.tsx is the splat child of the pathless layout. Measured over HTTP against the production build: /nope/deep/path and /circles render the shell; /login, /register, /invite/abc123 are not yet routes (Group 9) so they land on the same splat — the shell's absence there is not observable until those routes exist, which is the approved group order.

Measured in Chrome against the production build at three viewports. 390x844: side-nav display:none / width 0, bottom-nav display:block / height 61. 1230x560 and 1230x900: side-nav display:flex / 264px, bottom-nav display:none. Never both. The choice is CSS (nav:hidden / hidden nav:flex), so display:none also removes the other from the accessibility tree — no duplicate 'Navegación principal' landmark.

Four equal columns measured 95.5px x 56px each (≥44 on both axes) after the px-1 fix. padding-bottom resolves to max(env(safe-area-inset-bottom), 4px) — 4px measured on a notchless viewport.

not-found.pod.tsx mobile wrapper computes padding-bottom: 140px (pb-[8.75rem]) — measured, matching the 140 the contract names for NotFound-M. The bar is 61px tall with top at 783; the CTA's bottom is 592.8, so 190px of clearance, and the reserve is on the min-h-dvh wrapper, so content cannot extend into the last 140px even when it grows. /profile's 100px is Group 12's.

Measured rail: 264px wide, border-right 1px, position sticky, three stacked parts. Wordmark 34px mark (size-[2.125rem]) linking /circles at the top; three sections; identity row (avatar sm + «Sofía Martín») above a top border, href /profile. Four seeded circles render with their covers (/mock/circle-*.jpg).

Checked item for item in the served bytes, not inferred: «Mis círculos» x3 vs «Círculos» as the section label, «Privacidad» appears exactly once (rail only), «Perfil» exactly once (bar only). No user-icon item in the rail; the identity row is the profile entry. The two sets are not made to match.

side-nav.spec.tsx asserts the «Círculos» list is present with its cover when circles exist (getByRole('list', {name:'Círculos'})). Confirmed live: four circle rows in the rail at both desktop viewports.

side-nav.spec.tsx asserts the section is omitted entirely on an empty list — both the list role and the bare text «Círculos» are absent — and that the other four items plus the identity row survive. The Implementer's probe making the section unconditional went red; the branch is real.

aria-current='page' is driven by the pod's esLaRutaActual, never by colour alone (the active item also changes font weight and, in the rail, gets a pill background). side-nav.spec.tsx asserts exactly one marked link, that it is the identity row and that its href is /profile. On the 404 the served HTML carries 0 occurrences of aria-current — the deepest match is /$, which is no item's href, so marking nothing is the truth. Browser-level observability of the /profile case waits on Group 12.

Both composites render <nav aria-label="Navegación principal"> with the name baked in rather than passed as a prop, and every item is a real <a href> through FutureLink. No div+onClick anywhere in either file.

The bar is position:fixed and neither composite registers a scroll, resize or matchMedia listener (read, not assumed). The only animation is the colour transition FutureLink carries: measured transition-property 'color, background-color', duration 0.15s, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) — §8 item 1 exactly. The <nav>'s own computed transition-property 'all' at duration 0s is the CSS initial value, not a transition-all utility; git grep transition-all over apps/web/src returns nothing.
